PV2 monitoring

exceptions, checks, the issue register, and what has run · published, so it carries volumes and verdicts and never what a run cost

Audit summary

Every row on this page is read from a table pv2.calcs.audit_roll wrote to data/calcs, and DATA_AUDIT.xlsx holds the same rows, so the page and the workbook cannot disagree. A green cell means a check ran and passed; a check that never ran is shown as exactly that.

The funnel

Cumulative: a country counts at a hop only if it cleared every hop before it, and each fall names who fell.

Validators, country by country

Six validators per country. advisory is a failure the country's config demoted; never configured means no source document was named for the check to read, which is the state of the fidelity gate for most countries.

Self-audit checks

Each recomputes a stored figure from its own inputs and shows both operands. Advisory in the run, so a failure here never turns a run report red; it does turn this row red.

Where a check cannot fail

A ceiling taken from the programme rows being tested cannot be exceeded by them; a denominator never cross-checked cannot disagree with the document; a head with no programme row has nothing to reconcile.

The issue register

Every known defect: what happened, why, and its status. An issue closed here is closed nowhere else.

What the suite asserts

Every check

Read from the record the suite writes beside its reports. A green tick is a check that ran and passed at the time named, not a claim about now.

Precision

Measured from the human marks on today's matches, decided marks only; unsure is excluded rather than counted against. The suite holds a floor of 0.85 once at least 20 decided marks exist.

Recall

What the reverse pass contributed, and why the rest was dropped. Recall is measured by the recall review instead: sampled rows of the budget documents, including those the model matched to nothing, so a link a person finds that the model did not is a measured miss.

How each run went

Invariant checks

Each recomputes a stored figure from its own inputs. These ask whether the panel agrees with itself; the suite's gates ask whether it agrees with the source documents.

What the run flagged

What was read

The files each country's figures were built from, with the checksum they had when this page was written.

Every matched programme-strategy pair

Biggest money first. A pair reached by both passes appears once per rationale, marked twice; the panel still credits it once, which is why the pair count is the lower of the two figures above. This is a view, not a marking tool: marks belong in the review pages, where they are stored under the match's id and reach the numbers.

What has run

One row per run of the six entry-point scripts, newest first, from data/logs/runs.jsonl. Every script writes its line through runlog whether it passed or failed, so a run missing here is a run that never started. The log column is the file under data/logs/ holding that run's console output.

What was asked of the model

Per country and stage, summed over every real run: calls made, answers served from the cache instead, tokens in and out, and errors. Dry runs are excluded because they make no call. What a run cost is in the ledger on disk and is deliberately not here.

Azure Document Intelligence

Pages actually parsed against pages served from the parse cache, per country, over every real run. A country whose parsed count is 0 and whose cached count is high is being read entirely from cache, which is the steady state; a parsed count that keeps climbing means documents are being re-read.

Built 2026-09-10 from data/calcs. The internal monitoring page: it carries volumes and verdicts, never what a run cost.
